alex: Quick noise — after landing the batching_threshold=8 tweak we rolled yesterday, our perf tests show a consistent ~12% regression for small-seq matmuls (seq=64, batch=4) on the 80G nodes. nvtx/perfetto trace attached: https://perfetto.link/trace/abc123 :eyes:

maria: Which part regressed? end-to-end or just GEMM kernels?

alex: Short summary: end-to-end latency up ~12%. Kernel timeline shows GEMM kernels taking ~25% more wall time in the hot path. There's a pattern where cuBLASLt picks a different algo and then we see repeated workspace alloc/free storms between streams.

jon: Can you paste the nvtx snippet and the cublasLt logs? small things like workspace size falling back are usually obvious in the logs.

alex: Pasted below — nvtx ranges show `prepare_kv` -> `pack_inputs` -> `matmul_launch`. Right before `matmul_launch` there is a ~6ms gap where we do workspace alloc and cudaMemset.

```
[PERFETTO HIGHLIGHT]
nvtx: range_start("prepare_kv")  0.000s
nvtx: range_end("prepare_kv")    0.004s
nvtx: range_start("pack_inputs")  0.004s
nvtx: range_end("pack_inputs")    0.009s
nvtx: range_start("matmul_launch") 0.015s   <-- 6ms gap allocated
CUDA Kernel: cublasLtMatmulAlgoSearch 0.021s duration 0.006s
cublasLt: chosen algo_id=7 workspace=98304 bytes
cublasLt: fallback to algo_id=2 workspace=0 bytes (allocation failed)
```

alex: That allocation/fallback happens repeatedly when concurrency > 5. When concurrency is low we take algo_id=7 with workspace and performance is good. When concurrency > threshold, we keep falling back to workspace-free algo and see slower kernels.

kevin: Hmm — did the batching_threshold change cause more live streams to try to reserve workspace concurrently? We don't currently pool workspace per-GPU, it's per-stream right now.

sam: I repro'd locally. With `--simulate-concurrency 8` the workspace allocator contends and cudaMalloc retries show up in logs. Repro script: `./tools/run_matmul_micro --seq 64 --bs 4 --streams 8 --trace nvtx`

maria: Is cuBLASLt returning CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED or are we detecting allocation failure on our side? The log shows fallback to algo 2 which is workspace-free. If it's cublas throwing alloc error we need to switch to pooled allocator.

alex: Logs show fallback text from our wrapper, but underlying cudaMalloc returned OOM transiently (not persistent). We suspect fragmentation because many small allocations for KV cache + per-batch temp buffers are interleaved with workspace allocs.

perf-bot: Perf regression alert: matmul small-batch 64x4 increased 11.8% on ci/runtime-perf (compare 1765400000 -> 1765432098). Linking traces: https://perfetto.link/trace/abc123

jon: Proposed fixes: 1) implement a lightweight per-GPU contiguous workspace pool that services cublasLt requests (fast path), 2) change batching heuristic so we cap concurrent streams attempting workspace-heavy algos (degrade earlier), 3) probe for alternative algos that trade a bit more compute for less workspace to avoid fallback thrash.

kevin: I can work on a pooled workspace allocator. Quick plan: pre-alloc N MB per-GPU at startup (configurable), serve suballocations with simple bump allocator + free list. Hook into cublasLt wrapper so `allocate_workspace()` uses pool first, fallback to cudaMalloc if pool exhausted.

sam: For the heuristic, maybe track recent success rate of workspace algos per-stream and if failure rate > 30% within a sliding window, throttle new streams to the workspace path. That prevents herd effects.

maria: Also add NVTX markers around allocator slow paths so perf folk can see contention in traces. e.g., `nvtxRangeStart("ws_alloc")` before suballoc and `nvtxRangeEnd("ws_alloc")` after.

alex: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: roll back batching_threshold OR add a config to prefer workspace-free algos when concurrency > 6. Long-term: pooled allocator + heuristic + better cublasLt algo probing.

kevin: I'll prototype pool this afternoon. Sam can you add telemetry hooks and a perf test that runs streams=8/12/16 matrix shapes?

sam: On it — will add a CI job to capture traces and auto-diff kernel timeline.

jon: Also let's capture `cublasLtMatmulPreference` probing outputs in the logs (algo_id, workspace_bytes, estimated_time) so we can offline-analyze which algos were considered.

alex: Thanks everyone. Action items: kevin=pool POC, sam=telemetry + CI trace jobs, maria=add nvtx markers + log verbosity, jon=write up follow-up RFC for heuristic. I'll open a PR to pin batching_threshold while we iterate. :thumbsup: 

perf-bot: Created issue RT-3245 linking traces and perf job diffs.
